title: Every Anthropic tool call reaches the runtime with input={}: the adapter emits tool_use at content_block_start, before any argument JSON has streamed
repro: Real anthropic SDK 0.100.0 + httpx.MockTransport replaying the documented tool-use SSE shape (content_block_start tool_use input:{} -> input_json_delta '{"symbol": "RELI' -> 'ANCE.NS"}' -> content_block_stop) through AnthropicProvider.stream_chat -> output 'tool_use get_quote {}' then 'done tool_use'. The runtime then dispatches price_data/fundamentals/etc with no symbol on every Anthropic round. Script: scratchpad anth_proof.py
notes: Mechanism: _translate_event returns LLMToolUseEvent on content_block_start using block.input, which the Messages API always streams as {} - the arguments arrive afterwards as input_json_delta fragments that the translator drops (it only handles text_delta/thinking_delta). The SDK already accumulates the full input and fires a content_block_stop event carrying the finished block (_messages.py:406-416), so the fix is one branch. The unit test hides the bug: it fakes a content_block_start whose input is already {'symbol':'AAPL'} (test_llm_anthropic.py:166-172), a shape the real API never sends - special-casing to satisfy a test. Consequence: on Anthropic (listed in _PLANNER_PROVIDERS as a first-class provider, default claude-opus-4-8) every argumented tool runs empty; symbol-keyed handlers return 'missing symbol' so the model loops to _MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS, and optional-arg tools (news, market_overview) silently run on defaults and get narrated as the answer to the user's question. Distinct from COD-llm-adapters-1 (malformed-args coercion): here well-formed args are discarded 100% of the time. Smallest fix: emit the tool_use event on content_block_stop from event.content_block (type tool_use) instead of on content_block_start; replace the test fixture with the real start(input={}) -> input_json_delta -> stop sequence.

title: Groq and xAI are declared provider-level native-search providers, so the runtime withholds the local web_search tool - but the Groq adapter drops the flag and xAI sends a retired Live Search param
repro: native_search_available('groq', None, 'llama-3.3-70b-versatile') -> True (also True for 'xai'); agent_runtime then sets web_search=True and removes 'web_search' from tool_ids. Capturing GroqProvider's request with tool_ids=['price_data','news'], web_search=True -> request keys ['messages','model','stream','tools'], tools=['price_data','news'] - no search of any kind. A Groq user asking 'latest news on RELIANCE' gets an agent with neither native nor local web search. Script: scratchpad search_proof.py
evidence: sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:62, sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:186-187, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1334-1340, sidecar/config.py:364-388, sidecar/services/llm/groq.py:109-117, sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:690-695, sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:132-140, src/lib/model-options.ts:61-63, https://docs.x.ai/docs/guides/live-search (now serves the Web Search tool page: 'client.responses.create( model = "grok-4.7" ... tools = [ { "type" : "web_search" } ]'), https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/legacy/chat-completions ('Chat Completions is offered as a legacy endpoint. New features will come to the Responses API first.')
notes: Duplicated truth that already drifted: PROVIDER_LEVEL_NATIVE_SEARCH asserts 'every routable model rides the provider's own search' for groq, but groq.py:109-117 says the opposite in its own comment ('On a non-Compound Groq model there is no native search, so this is a graceful no-op (the runtime falls back to a BYOK search plugin)') - the runtime does NOT fall back; it removed the tool at agent_runtime.py:1340 on the default tier_a (config.py:388). The registry's only Groq models (llama-3.3-70b-versatile, llama-3.1-8b-instant) are non-Compound. xAI: the adapter injects extra_body.search_parameters (openai.py:691-695), the chat-completions Live Search surface; xAI's docs no longer document it anywhere (the old live-search URL now serves the Responses-API web_search tool, chat completions is labelled legacy) - live rejection vs silent ignore not confirmed here (no xAI key used), but in either case the local tool is gone. The picker compounds it: modelSearchPip tells the user non-OpenRouter providers 'never grow a pip' because 'the app's own search tool handles it' (model-options.ts:61-63), which is false for these two. In a product whose moat is research quality, an agent that silently cannot search on two of eight providers is a core-flow degrade. Smallest fix: make native_search_available per-model for groq (only compound-* ids) and drop xai from PROVIDER_LEVEL_NATIVE_SEARCH until the adapter speaks the Responses web_search tool; keep the local web_search tool whenever the adapter will not actually inject a native affordance.

title: Every Gemini agent round sends function_declarations together with google_search, a combination Google documents as Gemini-3-only, while the registry default is gemini-2.5-pro
repro: Agent invoke on provider gemini, default model gemini-2.5-pro, default tier_a -> native_search_available('gemini') is True -> web_search=True + agent tool_ids -> captured GeminiProvider request config.tools = [['function_declarations'], ['google_search']] (scratchpad search_proof.py). Needs-live-check: one agent invoke with a real Gemini key on gemini-2.5-pro should show whether the round 400s or silently drops one tool set.
evidence: sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:118-129, sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:62, sidecar/services/llm/native_search.py:186-187, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1334-1340, sidecar/config/model_registry.json (gemini default_model gemini-2.5-pro), sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:67-83, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/tool-combination.md.txt (line 2: 'Built-in and custom tools combinations are in Preview and supported for Gemini 3 models only.'), https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/google-search.md.txt ('Gemini 3 models also support combining these built-in tools with custom tools (function calling).')
notes: Same wrong truth table as COD-llm-adapters-2-2 (PROVIDER_LEVEL_NATIVE_SEARCH treats gemini as unconditionally native), with a worse failure shape: the adapter ORs the grounding tool into the same config.tools list as the agent's function declarations on every tool-capable round. On the default 2.5 model Google documents the combination as unsupported, so either the round is rejected (agent dead on Gemini) or one tool family is dropped (agent loses either its data tools or its search) - neither is surfaced. The one family that does support the combination (Gemini 3) relies on signatures carried on function_call parts ('signature ... Found on ... all tool call (e.g., function_call) and result (e.g., function_response) steps for Gemini 3+ models', tool-combination.md.txt:189); the adapter rebuilds the replayed model turn from {name,args} only (gemini.py:74-82) and never reads a signature off the stream, so the multi-round combination is lossy there too. Smallest fix: gate Gemini native search per-model (gemini-3* only) exactly like openai_native_search_supported, keep the local web_search tool otherwise; carry the raw function_call part (incl. thought_signature) through metadata for replay.

title: Key validation is wrong for three of eight providers: OpenRouter accepts any string, Gemini and xAI report a bad key as a 'transport error'
repro: get_provider('openrouter').validate_key('not-a-real-key') -> True (live call; openrouter.ai/api/v1/models answers 200 with or without auth, while /api/v1/key answers 401 'User not found.' for the same key). get_provider('gemini').validate_key('AIzaSyNOTAREALKEY...') -> raises ClientError 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT 'API key not valid' -> POST /llm/keys/validate returns ok=false detail='transport error: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. {...}'. curl api.x.ai/v1/models with a fake bearer -> HTTP 400 {"code":"invalid-argument","error":"Incorrect API key provided..."} -> openai.BadRequestError, not AuthenticationError -> same 'transport error' path.
evidence: sidecar/services/llm/openai.py:842-855, sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:186-204, sidecar/routers/llm.py:99-111, src/components/KeyEntryDialog.tsx:64-82, sidecar/services/errors.py:165-171, sidecar/services/llm/base.py:109-118
notes: The base contract defines 'invalid key' as HTTP 401/403 (base.py:113-116) and every adapter implements it that way, but the probe/status mapping is provider-specific and nobody checked it per provider. OpenRouter (the recommended broker lane) is the worst case: its /models is a public catalog, so the Key Entry Dialog says 'valid' and writes a typo'd or revoked key to the keychain (KeyEntryDialog.tsx:79); the user discovers it as a 401 in the middle of their first research turn. Gemini/xAI signal a bad key with 400, so validate_key re-raises and the dialog tells the user their network is broken; the same 400 also misses humanize's auth branch (errors.py:165) on the chat stream, so a bad Gemini/xAI key never gets the 'key was rejected - check Settings' message either. Distinct from COD-llm-adapters-9 (raw exception text): humanize alone would not fix this, the classification itself is wrong. Smallest fix: OpenRouter probes GET /key (authenticated); Gemini/xAI treat 400 with API_KEY_INVALID / 'Incorrect API key' as False; add the same mapping to humanize.

title: Tool-call ids are not unique for Ollama ('' for every call) or Gemini (name_index, reset per round), and the process-global host-action ack ledger is keyed on them
repro: (a) Ollama (the store's defaultProviderId): SDK ToolCall has no id field, adapter emits tool_call_id='' -> frontend ackHostAction returns early on an empty id and ActionAckRequest requires min_length=1 -> every AUTO host action (set_chart_symbol, open_panel, write_note...) is rewritten to status 'dispatched_unconfirmed' ('do not report it as done') after a 0.8 s grace wait, every round. (b) Gemini: round 1 set_chart_symbol gets id 'set_chart_symbol_0', panel acks 'applied'; round 2 (or any run within the 600 s TTL) issues set_chart_symbol again -> same id -> _await_host_action_acks finds the stale entry immediately and the model is told the NEW action 'applied' before the panel has processed it (or even if it later keeps_previous).
evidence: sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:206-215, sidecar/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/ollama/_types.py:333-352, sidecar/services/llm/ollama.py:89-90, sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:140-163, sidecar/services/action_ledger.py:25-31, sidecar/services/action_ledger.py:80-87, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1065-1080, sidecar/services/agent_runtime.py:1618-1625, sidecar/routers/agents.py:44-64, src/lib/host-actions.ts:1452-1458, src/store/llm-providers.ts:135
notes: Uniqueness of tool_call_id is an unstated invariant every consumer relies on (OpenAI/Groq tool pairing, the ack ledger, publish_brief_calls, the grounded read-back) but no adapter is required to produce it: Ollama passes through a field its SDK does not have, Gemini mints f'{name}_{tool_call_index}' with the counter reset per stream (gemini.py:142), and the leak rescue hardcodes 'leaked-0' (COD-llm-adapters-11). COD-llm-adapters-11 was downgraded because no consumer was shown to break; this is that consumer: action_ledger is process-global with a 10-minute TTL, so a non-unique id either can never be acked (Ollama) or matches another action's ack (Gemini), and the R13 grounded read-back - built so the model never claims an unconfirmed panel change - becomes wrong in both directions. Ollama tool-result turns also omit tool_name (ollama.py:89-90) although the SDK Message has it, so a round with two calls gives the local model no way to pair results. Smallest fix: define the invariant in one place - LLMToolUseEvent gets a default_factory uuid id or base.py exposes ensure_call_id() that every adapter calls when the provider id is empty/synthetic; pass metadata['name'] as tool_name on Ollama tool turns.

title: Gemini usage omits thinking tokens, so the BudgetGuard spend/token ceiling under-meters every Gemini 2.5 round
repro: Gemini 2.5 Pro round that thinks 6k tokens and answers 800 -> usage_metadata.candidates_token_count=800, thoughts_token_count=6000 -> adapter reports output_tokens=800 -> BudgetGuard.record folds 800 + input; the user's key is billed for 6800 output tokens.
evidence: sidecar/services/llm/gemini.py:167-173, sidecar/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/google/genai/types.py:7796-7826 (total_token_count 'is the sum of prompt_token_count, candidates_token_count, tool_use_prompt_token_count, and thoughts_token_count'), sidecar/services/budget_guard.py:116-133, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking.md.txt ('When thinking is turned on, response pricing is the sum of output tokens and thinking tokens.')
notes: The adapter is the only place that knows the provider's usage schema, and it drops two of the four billed components (thoughts_token_count, and tool_use_prompt_token_count from google_search grounding). The registry marks these prices as §6.5-adjacent because they meter the Delegate spend ceiling (model_registry.json prices._comment); for the default gemini-2.5-pro, which always thinks, thinking tokens routinely dominate output, so a detached Delegate run can blow well past its configured USD/token ceiling before BudgetGuard trips. Anthropic and OpenAI-shaped adapters are fine (their output/completion counts include reasoning). Smallest fix: output_tokens = candidates + thoughts, input_tokens = prompt + tool_use_prompt (or read total_token_count).

title: Anthropic output is hard-capped at 4096 tokens and no layer treats a max_tokens/length finish as truncation
repro: Deep-research synthesis or a long agent answer on Anthropic -> adapter sends max_tokens=4096 (no caller ever sets max_tokens) -> the stream stops mid-sentence with stop_reason 'max_tokens' -> LLMDoneEvent.finish_reason='max_tokens' -> oneshot.complete returns the partial text as the synthesis, agent_runtime only inspects finish_reason=='content_filter', the UI decodes finishReason and never reads it -> a cut-off brief is rendered as complete.
notes: DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS is commented 'Conservative default' but it is the ONLY value ever sent - grep finds no caller passing max_tokens (the runtime allowlists it at agent_runtime.py:102 and nobody fills it). Current Claude models allow far larger outputs; 4096 is small for a multi-section equity brief. The general half is provider-agnostic: finish_reason rides LLMDoneEvent all the way to the browser and is never acted on, so truncation on any provider is silent. In a research product a truncated synthesis presented as final is the data-trust failure the brief UI is built to avoid. Smallest fix: raise the Anthropic default to the model's documented output ceiling (or pass it from the registry), and have oneshot/runtime flag finish_reason in {'max_tokens','length'} as a visible 'answer truncated' note.
